deviations.supervisor_behaviour_assessment: CORRECT. research_workflow/supervisor/core.py:776-779 routes a BLOCKED/PLATFORM_DEFECT worker result straight to _escalate, and the repair packet (core.py:566-572) explicitly instructs the worker not to fix shared platform code in the study branch. Escalating after one repair attempt is the designed behaviour for this blocker class, not a retry-accounting bug. attempts values are all <= 2.

deviations.what: The read-only worker tool allowlist does not include the PowerShell tool, and its Bash entries are prefix-scoped, so a read-only auditor's attempts to run the MANDATED result-card command were denied. The causal auditor recorded 6 permission denials (5 of them the `python scripts/research.py study result ...` command issued through the PowerShell tool) before it got the card written; the contract auditor recorded 1 (a compound `cd ... && echo ...` Bash command).
deviations.where_observed: research_workflow/supervisor/providers.py build_command, read_only branch: --allowedTools Read Grep Glob Write 'Bash(python scripts/research.py:*)' 'Bash(git status:*)' 'Bash(git log:*)' 'Bash(git diff:*)'; --disallowedTools Edit NotebookEdit
deviations.evidence: permission_denials arrays in logs/002_causal_audit_6b6cdc45.log (6) and logs/003_contract_audit_182864f7.log (1); 0 in both write-capable workers' logs
deviations.impact: Both auditors recovered and wrote DONE cards, so nothing failed. But on Windows the harness's primary shell tool is PowerShell, and the packet mandates a CLI call, so every read-only worker burns turns rediscovering that it must use Bash. A worker close to its wall-clock cap could hit WORKER_TIMEOUT for this reason alone.
deviations.side_effect_positive: This is also the strongest available proof for evidence item (h): the auditors demonstrably ran under a restricted tool set and NOT under --dangerously-skip-permissions, while the design and repair workers ran with 0 denials.

deviations.what: The supervisor launches the controller as `sys.executable <canonical repo>/scripts/run_governed_study.py --study <study worktree>/studies/<id>` with cwd = the study worktree. Because run_governed_study.py puts ITS OWN root (the canonical checkout) on sys.path, the platform modules that are loaded, executed and hashed into the execution closure come from `main`, while the study contract lives on the study branch in a different checkout. Nothing records or enforces that the two agree.
deviations.evidence: The contract auditor read _work/controller/status.json while it recorded worktree {branch: main, head: a33b1460, path: <canonical>}; test_summary.json file paths were all under the canonical checkout. Independently confirmed in source. (The status.json now on disk records the study worktree because the repair worker re-ran the bounded check by hand from inside it.)
deviations.impact_this_run: BENIGN. git diff a33b1460..c49d8140 touches only studies/supv1_shape_a_flip_180s/, so every closure file is byte-identical in both checkouts and composite a563bbf1... is valid for this study at this commit.
deviations.impact_general: A study worktree that carried merged platform work main lacked would have current_composite() resolved from main's bytes and compared against a freeze also written from main's bytes: R9 and EXECUTION_MANIFEST would agree with each other and both would be wrong for the study. Remediation suggested by the contract auditor: record the resolving checkout's head in frozen_execution_manifest.json and fail readiness when it differs from the study worktree head.
